name: @aztec-avm-runtime/browser
description: Browser packaging for the AVM runtime — built by build.mjs, never by npm
//: THIS FILE DECLARES WHAT WAS ALREADY TRUE AND ADDS NOTHING ELSE. Every source under `src/` and
`demo/` is an ES module, `build.mjs` is `.mjs`, and esbuild has always treated this tree as
ESM by content. What was missing was the DECLARATION, and nothing needed it until a
TYPE-CHECKED package imported from here.
WHY IT APPEARED NOW. The live-chain replay campaign's browser AVM host reuses
`browser/src/loader.ts` rather than re-implementing 570 lines of WASI shim — the loader is
dependency-free (node-host plus its own wasi.ts, no @aztec), so nothing crosses the npm-pin
boundary between the two packages. But `replay/tsconfig.json` is `module: NodeNext` with
`verbatimModuleSyntax`, THIS REPOSITORY HAS NO ROOT package.json, and `browser/` had none —
so tsc read `browser/src/wasi.ts` as CommonJS and refused its exports with TS1287. `browser/`
has no tsconfig and is type-checked by no recipe; this is the first time anything has asked
tsc what these files are.
AND IT WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE SIBLING CAMPAIGN'S BUILD BEFORE BEING ADDED, IN THE CHECKOUT
WHERE THAT BUILD ACTUALLY RUNS. `just browser-build` passes every recorded gzipped budget with
this file present — seven entries, unchanged. An earlier attempt appeared to break it, but that
was measured in a worktree with no `orchestration/node_modules` install where the build had
never worked at all; the conclusion was withdrawn rather than acted on.
NO DEPENDENCIES, DELIBERATELY, AND NO `npm ci` STEP. `build.mjs` resolves `@aztec/*` through
`orchestration/node_modules` and esbuild through `spike/` or `diffsim/`. Declaring dependencies
here would create a second install of a pinned line, which is the hazard `pins.json` exists for.
